assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
The attached image is the user's ACTUAL blade ion trap mechanical reference. Create a new clear scientific educational illustration based faithfully on this reference. Do NOT use the generic four cylindrical rod trap.
Preserve recognizable structure: a circular metal mounting flange at the bottom; a short cylindrical open cage pedestal with vertical support pillars; above it a small dark-gray perforated cylindrical mounting block; two tall upright gray machined side supports left and right forming a vertical U-shaped assembly; a thin vertical light cyan blade-chip substrate with patterned gold triangular inward-facing electrode tips in the central upper gap; small copper bent leads and blue insulated cap electrodes at both sides; one slender diagonal atom oven tube at upper right pointing toward the central chip.
Composition: left two-thirds show the assembled reference-derived trap in three-quarter view, full pedestal and flange visible. Right third show a magnified conceptual inset of just the central gold blade tips facing a small trapping gap, a violet dot marked "Ion" and a dashed cross marked "RF null" slightly displaced, plus a small double arrow marked "EMM". Draw a thin violet straight line across this inset marked "Probe laser"; only within the inset, not through opaque mechanical supports. A thin leader links the real chip region to the inset.
Use a refined editorial technical illustration, warm white background, steel gray mechanical body, pale cyan substrate, gold electrodes, violet light, teal motion symbols. Short English labels only: "Blade chip", "Endcap 1", "Endcap 2", "Atomic oven", "Ion", "RF null", "EMM", "Probe laser". No title, no numeric dimensions, no claimed electrical RF/DC labels, no formulas, no logos, no watermarks. The inset is qualitative, not a reconstruction of hidden internal geometry. Maintain actual vertical chip design and overall shapes in reference. Do not turn it into horizontal rod electrodes or a surface trap on a horizontal PCB. Wide 3:2 landscape.
assets.edit: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the provided reference-derived blade-trap educational illustration. Preserve the entire left mechanical assembly, exact general appearance, all labels, white background, layout and gold blade inset. Make ONLY the micromotion geometry in the right inset unambiguous: move the dashed "RF null" cross onto the same horizontal centerline as the violet Ion dot, slightly to the right of it. Replace the vertical teal double-headed EMM arrow by a horizontal teal double-headed arrow directly below the ion, parallel to the horizontal purple Probe laser beam. EMM label below that arrow. RF null label remains legible, leader points to the dashed cross. This portrays a detectable micromotion projection along the laser. Do not change any other part.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create an educational scientific diagram of RF-photon correlation detection. Use the attached photograph as the mechanical reference for the small "Blade trap" illustration: vertical cyan and gold blade chip between two upright metal posts, round pedestal and circular flange. No rod trap. White background, navy labels, teal electronics paths, violet photon path, clean flat vector-like raster infographic, wide 3:2.
Keep signal topology extremely simple and precise:
Top left block "RF pickup"; below left block "Photon detector". Both separate arrows point to ONE center block "Time tagger". RF pickup arrow labeled "RF phase"; detector arrow labeled "Photon times".
At far left top, small RF waveform feeds RF pickup. At far left bottom, small blade trap based on reference with a violet ion dot and photons going through a collection lens to Photon detector.
One arrow from Time tagger to right-hand block "Fold by RF phase"; show a single-period conceptual sinusoidal histogram inside. One arrow down from that block to bottom right block "Fit X and Y". One arrow left from Fit X and Y to bottom center block "Choose DC voltages". END here, no feedback wire, no loop. Bottom note "Repeat measurement after each voltage step".
Title "From photons to compensation".
Small trap illustration labeled "Blade trap". Text only exactly these labels. No equations, no numerical ticks or values. All boxes separate, all labels readable, no extra connections.
